feature: Version-tolerant keyed language packs, layered fonts and RTL shaping
assessment: RIPPS2 uses English-text hashes with fallback and adds Arabic/Persian joining/bidi plus Lao marks/wrapping. RiptOPL remains positional; printf-format validation already exists and is not counted as missing.

feature: Declarative HTML/CSS flexbox compilation and reusable C99 console UI runtime
assessment: OPHTML compiles layouts to a bounded zero-allocation GS command list and publishes a reusable launcher-core archive; RiptOPL uses its existing theme configuration engine.

feature: Pre-resolved pairwise HarfBuzz kerning
assessment: Font shaping/kerning data is prepared off-console for EE use; separate from having UTF-8 fonts.

feature: Palette-index theme switching without texture re-upload
assessment: Specific instant color-scheme mechanism rather than ordinary theme switching.

feature: Runtime 2D layout-coordinate offsets for animated expansion
assessment: OPHTML runtime layout primitive, beyond RiptOPL's element-specific carousel/list animations.

feature: Focus-subtree visibility masking with automatic navigation bypass
assessment: A coordinated layout/focus-tree mechanism, not simply hiding one image.

feature: Bounded binary UI loading and compiler budgets for declarative themes
assessment: Fuzzed .uib parsing, alignment checks and hard input/layout safety limits for OPHTML's format. Different architecture; not proof of an exploitable RiptOPL theme bug.

feature: Animated game-launch presentation beyond black fade
assessment: RiptOPL has launch/video black fades; PS2-Launcher and Titan have their own staged launch animations. Retained as optional presentation, not missing handoff correctness.

feature: Write debug logs to a BDM storage device
assessment: Historical uOPL logging output, distinct from RiptOPL's network/debug logging.

feature: Neutrino in-game return/IGR
assessment: RiptOPL has OPL-core IGR; the bundled Neutrino does not implement LUNA's held-combo return path.

feature: Coordinated Neutrino power-button shutdown
assessment: Optical-work drain and DEV9 shutdown on the physical power event; separate from the OPL-core power path.

feature: Neutrino VMC backing and management for APA/PFS games
assessment: RiptOPL supports native-core VMC on APA, but deliberately drops Neutrino APA VMC arguments. LUNA's mapped backing has geometry and fragment limits; save/reload testing remains necessary.

feature: Grouped PS1 disc sets, starting-disc picker and in-game swaps
assessment: LUNA implements ordered two-to-four-VCD sets and swaps in its matching runtime; FastLoader claims an Ember starting-disc picker. RiptOPL's ordinary PS1 listing is already present.

feature: Named PS1 card pairs with import/export, paired backups and recovery
assessment: The missing capability is the integrated pair-management lifecycle, beyond existing POPStarter/Ember saves and basic card creation.

feature: Browse save images and import/export PSU or copy card pairs
assessment: Integrated VMC-as-folder/PSU tools and confirmed absent-destination PS1 pair copies; RiptOPL can create/assign cards but does not expose these save-browser operations.

feature: Physical memory-card backup, restore, format and repair UI
assessment: Other shells integrate these tools. Optional extension with destructive operations, rather than a missing ability to save a game.

feature: Paused in-game actions menu with resume, return and power off
assessment: RIPPS2 now enables its panel by default and adds power off; Titan has profile-gated suspend/resume, and LUNA integrates a native PS1 Quit/Play return panel. RiptOPL's reset and RA notices do not provide these menus.

feature: Rip optical discs directly to the library or media storage
assessment: RIPDISC now exists in builds 105-110: PS2 ISO/split output, PS1 BIN/CUE, audio CD and DVD-video paths. Previous planned status is obsolete; emulator reports are not PS2 acceptance.

feature: Managed in-game screenshot capture and artwork development
assessment: RIPSHOT has six-slot rolls, preview/Keep/Delete, ART/MEDIA output, PNG development and SCRn slideshow. RiptOPL inherits optional IGS code, so the gap is this complete managed workflow, not the existence of screenshot code.

feature: Integrated multi-device file explorer and bulk operations
assessment: Copy/move tray, rename/delete/mkdir, conflict choices, verified moves, text preview and ELF launch. Launchstation can supply file management externally; it is not embedded in RiptOPL.

feature: Cross-device file/folder search that opens the matching location
assessment: RIPPS2 build 107 implements bounded breadth-first search, cancellation and result navigation; it is no longer merely planned.

feature: Coordinated game-file rename with art, VMC and metadata migration
assessment: FastLoader claims renaming the ISO carries its associated assets, card and settings; display-title editing in RiptOPL is already available.

feature: Automatic ISO discovery throughout arbitrary folder trees
assessment: FastLoader claims four-level discovery outside CD/DVD. RiptOPL's prefix/subfolder navigation is not a whole-drive arbitrary-directory scan.

feature: Persistent per-source game-list snapshots with idle revalidation
assessment: RIPPS2 caches MMCE/BDM/SMB lists on their source. RiptOPL already has ISO-ID and APA list caches; the missing scope is its equivalent across those other backends.

feature: One settings-destination picker that provisions typed device paths
assessment: RIPPS2 offers MC/HDD/USB/MX4SIO/iLink/MMCE and creates its folder. RiptOPL already supports custom/typed paths; this is the guided workflow, not new settings-storage support.

feature: Recently played history containing multiple games
assessment: OPLattice retains the last eight, rather than only RiptOPL's remembered last title.

feature: User-selectable alphabetical, reverse, recent and scan-order sorting
assessment: Distinct from remembering a selected game and from PS1/PS2 filters.

feature: Per-game launch counts and accumulated play time
assessment: A play-history/statistics layer, beyond a last-played selection.

feature: One automatically aggregated library across every game device
assessment: RiptOPL's Favorites can span sources and its platform filters mix PS1/PS2; neither aggregates all non-favorite games from every source into one library.

feature: Favorites stored per game drive and carried with that drive
assessment: RiptOPL deliberately uses a shared cross-device favorites file. This is an alternative persistence policy, not missing Favorites.

feature: Staged replacement and recovery for last-title and title-ID cache files
assessment: Favorites staging/recovery already exists in RiptOPL. Only LUNA's additional last-title/cache coverage remains to compare and extend.

feature: Choose among multiple discovered UDPFS servers
assessment: Modulo exposes server selection; RiptOPL automatically chooses a server. Existing network-game transport is not missing.

feature: Generic backend/path forward-boot command line including no-init
assessment: NHDDL accepts mode/DVD-path forwarding and reuse of the resident environment; RiptOPL's positional HDD/BDM autolaunch is narrower.

feature: Extended APA addressing for HDDs above 2 TiB
assessment: Different from existing exFAT/GPT large-drive support. Source integration and safe media layout need independent evaluation.

feature: EXT2 filesystem support on USB
assessment: E2OPL's legacy filesystem path is distinct from RiptOPL's FAT32/exFAT support; no current hardware regression claim.

feature: Selectable DKWDRV/PS1VModeNeg physical-PS1-disc handoff
assessment: RiptOPL has ordinary disc actions and PS1 image cores; this is the explicit enhanced-disc-launcher handoff workflow.

feature: Conditional import-disc OSD language override
assessment: The enhanced launcher applies an override conditionally for import-disc behavior.

feature: Download cover artwork directly on the PS2
assessment: PC artwork tools already work with RiptOPL; the missing operation is the console-initiated download.

feature: Broadcast a game-launch event for a Discord presence listener
assessment: A console launch-announcement interface, distinct from an external companion calculating presence by other means.

feature: DualSense over Bluetooth in menu and in-game PADEMU
assessment: RiptOPL already has an optional USB DualSense variant; Bluetooth support is the gap.

feature: Wireless device discovery, secure pairing and persisted link keys in the GUI
assessment: Distinct from existing DS3 cable pairing and stock DS3/DS4 Bluetooth input.

feature: Automatic RTL8761B/BU Bluetooth firmware loading
assessment: Menu and in-game dongle initialization in the Realtek fork.

feature: Extended DS4-clone HID, CRC, handshake and rumble handling
assessment: Additional clone protocol/feedback support; existing fake-DS3 workaround is not equivalent.

feature: Multi-pad connection/type/battery HUD and setup/test/disconnect UI
assessment: Combines overlapping pad-status rows rather than counting each fork's screen twice.

feature: Mixed physical/wireless multitap routing per slot and two-port poll
assessment: The rt-2.7.0 source splits real-pad transfers and preserves per-slot choices. RiptOPL has multitap emulation already; this is the additional routing behavior/fix.

feature: Xbox One and Series controllers over USB
assessment: Requires a controller driver/protocol beyond RiptOPL's DS3/DS4 and optional DS5 paths.

feature: Xbox 360 controllers over USB
assessment: Separate controller class from Xbox One/Series; implemented in historical modular PADEMU.

feature: Generic descriptor-driven USB HID gamepads
assessment: Generic report parsing, rather than only a whitelist of controller-specific drivers.

feature: Additional Steam Controller, Shanwan PS3 and GP300 USB support
assessment: Specific protocol/device coverage in PS2-Launcher, not a claim that every clone is supported there.

feature: USB Driving Force wheel presented as a negCon
assessment: An experimental wheel translation path, distinct from ordinary pad emulation.

feature: Xbox Bluetooth/BLE and USB keyboard/mouse input classes
assessment: Titan's modern-input contracts are source/host validated with target acceptance pending; BoliviaOS separately advertises USB keyboard input.

feature: Hold SELECT alone to leave a game
assessment: Alternative configurable exit interaction, beyond existing multi-button IGR.

feature: Two-axis flat tile-grid library navigation
assessment: RiptOPL's linear Coverflow and PSBBN perspective fan do not provide the same grid.

feature: Depth-sorted orbital ring library view
assessment: A complete selectable ring renderer with perspective and depth falloff.

feature: Projected 3D case grid with case styles and inspection
assessment: LUNA's projected case layout and PS1 case presentation; distinct from flat tiles and PSBBN Flow.

feature: Ambient-orb Scroll view with logo/title fallback and controls
assessment: A full browsing view, not a claim that RiptOPL lacks animation or missing-art text.

feature: Continuously rotating disc-label art and paired-art presentation
assessment: RiptOPL already supports ICO/LGO/COV artwork; animation is the differentiated capability.

feature: LUNA-specific view toggles, Random Scan and presentation presets
assessment: Includes view enablement, orbital auto-browsing, glass/font/background options; generic theme selection already exists in RiptOPL.

feature: SHELF dashboard/sidebar with Home, Library, Apps and Settings
assessment: An optional complete shell presentation rather than a new game source.

feature: Interpolated XMB category and game-list rails
assessment: Caduceus OPL's specific navigation model.

feature: Game-details card with automatic RA support/status checks
assessment: RiptOPL already has achievement support checks and a browser; the additional automatic details-card workflow remains different.

feature: Initialize manual devices asynchronously when their category receives focus
assessment: RiptOPL has manual and automatic discovery, but not this specific category-focus policy.

feature: Dedicated carousel/device dock and system-status HUD primitives
assessment: OPL FUTURE's optional interface architecture; no generalized console-performance claim.

feature: Unified controller, memory-card, storage and network dashboard
assessment: OPL Evolution's integrated status surface; ordinary individual status indicators overlap existing behavior.

feature: Configurable framebuffer blur/frosted-glass compositing
assessment: A new render/compositing primitive rather than an image that resembles blur.

feature: CardShelf element and crossfading cover-art wallpaper
assessment: Daniel's PS5-style theme primitives; generic carousel/artwork display already exists.

feature: Load an entire theme from a TAR archive
assessment: RiptOPL already loads ART/CFG/CHT archives; the missing archive type is THM/theme resources.

feature: Theme X-position controls specifically for widescreen layouts
assessment: wsX and x_scaled address the same broad layout requirement and are counted together.

feature: Live PADEMU/GSM/cheat-state icons supplied to themes
assessment: Distinct from static metadata badges in AttributeImage.

feature: Info-only page without list navigation
assessment: An alternative information-screen interaction policy.

feature: Bind image elements to non-selected neighboring game rows
assessment: Offset-driven hero/filmstrip layouts.

feature: MenuTabs strip showing all devices and custom labels
assessment: Existing MenuText/current-device selection is narrower.

feature: Theme-controlled game-count prefix and suffix
assessment: Current RiptOPL GameCountText uses the localized FILE_COUNT format.

feature: Per-app subtitle metadata and display
assessment: A separate subtitle field in the app's title.cfg.

feature: Per-row star, highlight and platform-decorator controls
assessment: RiptOPL has Favorites and decorators; the configurable star column/highlight/PS1/PS2/app controls are additional.

feature: Cycle startup backgrounds without repeats until the set is exhausted
assessment: Specific shuffle-bag behavior advertised by FastLoader, not basic background/theme support.

feature: Selectable suffix RA mark and a smaller unframed cover mark
assessment: RiptOPL still builds an RA prefix and has no gRABadgeSuffix choice. Alphabetic sorting must be checked separately before attributing a sorting bug.

feature: Independent graphics-enhancement files and selection
assessment: Titan separates ENH enhancements from gameplay CHT cheats, with separate per-game choices and metadata.

feature: Named system users whose selected profile chooses an exclusive VMC
assessment: Different from per-game card assignment alone.

feature: Notification center with retained activity/download progress
assessment: RiptOPL has transient notifications rather than a retained activity service.

feature: Installable native app packages and an in-process application SDK
assessment: Titan TPKG/runtime services; ordinary external ELF launching is already present.

feature: Integrated lightweight interactive web browser
assessment: HTTP text/link browsing and bridge-backed HTTPS, rather than HTTP game streaming.

feature: In-console staged/rollback-capable system updater
assessment: RiptOPL distributes release kits instead of performing transactional console installation.

feature: Repository catalog, dependency resolution and verified package downloads
assessment: Titan Store foundation; target download acceptance remains pending and no finished-storefront claim is made.

feature: Packaged scene/keyframe themes with transitions, idle loops and audio
assessment: More than existing OPL theme images, BGM and built-in animations.

feature: General-purpose console music player
assessment: Separate from RiptOPL background music playback.

feature: General-purpose image and font viewers
assessment: Separate from rendering game artwork and UI fonts.

feature: Integrated text/code editor and terminal
assessment: BoliviaOS tool suite, outside normal game launching.

feature: Integrated PDF viewer
assessment: A separate document-viewing application in the console shell.

feature: Retro-system ROM libraries with configured emulator/core launch
assessment: RETROLauncher and the Retro Arcade suite provide ROM catalogs beyond RiptOPL's PS1/PS2/Apps views; launching an emulator ELF through Apps already exists.

feature: Retro Arcade launch-mode picker and return to the selected ROM
assessment: The suite documents 240p/480i/480p selection and returning to the same game; not a new PS2 OPL/Neutrino compatibility mode.

feature: Select PSXCore as a third PS1 runtime / use its source-buildable adapter
assessment: RiptOPL ships POPStarter and Ember, not PSXCore. Main no longer ships tester sources; the tester branch is separate.

feature: Optional guarded decoded-instruction code validation
assessment: A PSXCore mechanism; different from RiptOPL checking file/module identities before launch.

feature: PSXCore GPU/GTE/DMA semantic corrections
assessment: Includes palette/query fixes, signed INTPL interpolation and parked-worker GP1 DMA-control changes. No inferred superiority for a particular game.

feature: PSXCore MDEC/RGB24/buffered-interlace corrections
assessment: Includes publishing the completed interlace display descriptor; not proof that all FMVs are fixed.

feature: PSXCore SPU, capture-IRQ, reverb and CDDA corrections
assessment: Alternative runtime implementation, not a claim RiptOPL has no PS1 audio.

feature: PSXCore guest-memory, CPU-timing and load-delay fast paths
assessment: Includes precomputed addressing and smaller DMA/GP0/GP1 saves now enabled by default, with disable switches retained.

feature: PSXCore firmware-identity and transactional runtime-patch planner
assessment: Includes byte guards, overlap/capacity checks and revision-specific license-string changes; no generic region-bypass claim.

feature: PSXCore native-save worker, PFS ownership and flush guards
assessment: Partially provisioned native-partition path; source mechanisms do not establish power-loss durability or a complete APA user flow.

feature: PSXCore disc/TOC fingerprint binding to save identity
assessment: A content-identity mechanism beyond ordinary file naming.

feature: Optional adaptive PCM output-rate feedback
assessment: Off by default, changes rate/possibly pitch; not a CPU-speed fix.

feature: PSXCore bounded sector-tail cache and seek-status correction
assessment: Runtime I/O mechanism; broad game-speed improvement is unmeasured.

feature: PSXCore exact raster/polygon-cost fast path
assessment: Keep timing/compatibility evidence separate from build success.

feature: PSXCore GP0 packet/callback/empty-flush fast paths
assessment: Source optimization, not a standalone proven end-user compatibility feature.

feature: PSXCore bounded aligned/unaligned upload-row copies
assessment: The newer branch streams rows with aligned quadword loads while retaining bounds.

feature: PSXCore boot/save-worker and patch-plan diagnostics
assessment: Current adapter also reports planner failures and increases its bounded capacity.
